$comment: Product backlog. Canonical machine state - automation reads this, not Markdown. Scores assist prioritisation only; the Project Manager, Client and Architect decide scope. A rejected item does not return without new evidence.

items.title: CI proves what deployment ships (v2-unit layer)
items.userProblem: A V2 regression reaches production undetected. The 49 tests covering the application that serves careerscope.tech run in no workflow.
acceptanceCriteria: A v2-unit CI job runs the no-services V2 tests on every push
The job states what it does NOT cover, so it cannot imply full V2 coverage
Proven: breaking a v2 unit test turns the job red
evidence: git grep 'npm test' .github/workflows -> ci.yml:76 and deploy.yml:73, both the ROOT suite only
v2 test script requires --env-file=.env; v2/.env is gitignored
ci.yml has no services: block
items.securityImpact: none directly; removes a blind spot in the release path
items.architectureImpact: CI topology only; no application change
items.summary: The application that actually runs the website had tests that no pipeline ever executed. Now the quick ones run on every change, so an obvious break is caught before it ships. The slower half still does not run — that is CS-9.

items.title: Lead table header offset is wrong on Linux WebKit at 768px
items.userProblem: The sticky header is 48px out on Safari at tablet width, so rows sit underneath it.
acceptanceCriteria: Reproduced in the Playwright Linux container, not guessed from Windows
Root cause named; the assertion is not widened
check-ui.mjs green on all three engines in CI
evidence: webkit: sticky offset mismatch at 768px - header 57, expected 105, delta -48.0000
57 = 3.5rem*16+1 and 105 = 6.5rem*16+1: two breakpoints apart, not a settle race
Passes on Windows WebKit (webkit-2359); CI runs Linux WebKit
items.summary: On one browser engine, the table header on the Leads page sits in the wrong place at tablet width, so it overlaps the rows you are trying to read. Two attempted fixes did not hold because both treated it as a timing fluke; it is not.

items.title: Proxy restart strands every service behind a healthy-looking 502
items.userProblem: The site can be entirely down while every container reports healthy.
acceptanceCriteria: A Caddy crash recovers without operator action, or is detected and alerted
Proven by killing Caddy and observing the result
evidence: restart-stack.sh is operator recovery, not self-healing
items.summary: If the web server in front of everything crashes, the whole site goes down while every internal health check still reports fine. Nobody is told. Fixing this means it either recovers by itself or you find out immediately.

items.title: Release publishes a stale version string when a version file is added
items.userProblem: Published Pages can claim a version that was never released.
acceptanceCriteria: The publish list is derived from versionFiles(), not duplicated
A test asserts every versionFiles key is staged
evidence: grep -rn 'mobile-site/version.js' scripts/*.mjs -> two independent lists
items.summary: When a new version file is added, the release can publish the old version number, so the site claims to be running something it is not.

items.title: Retire the V1 application layer
items.userProblem: Two application layers to maintain; only one ships.
acceptanceCriteria: Pages export reads PostgreSQL
MCP server runs against V2
apps/api and apps/web removed with CI green
evidence: Dockerfile copies only apps/api/package.json, for workspace resolution
scripts/export-mobile.mjs and export-admin.mjs read the V1 SQLite database
React is 19.2.8 in both trees - no dependency conflict keeps them apart
items.summary: The original first-generation application is still in the repository. Most of it is unused, but parts still feed the public job page, so it cannot simply be deleted. This is about untangling that safely.

items.title: Frontend route architecture, auth boundary and shared shell
items.userProblem: No deep links, no per-page loading or error states, no auth boundary. One 830-line page.tsx fakes navigation with a view variable.
acceptanceCriteria: Real routes
Auth boundary enforced
Shared shell
axe clean
evidence: 1 page.tsx in v2; UX/UI recorded at 15%
items.summary: The front-end pages grew one at a time, so navigation, the signed-in boundary and the shared page frame are inconsistent. This is the clean-up that makes new screens quick to add instead of copy-pasted.

completedSteps: Confirmed the real defect: the deploy gate is a strict subset of CI, never running check-ui.mjs, the V2 tests, Pages validation or root format:check
Corrected the plan: needs: cannot span workflows, so the Pages pattern could not be copied
Added the require-ci job querying the Actions API for the exact head SHA
Moved the decision into scripts/require-ci-success.mjs so it could be tested without a network or jq
Added scripts/check-deploy-gate.mjs: 22 checks, 5 mutations proven detected
Wired release, agile, deploy and agent gates into CI via npm run gates:test — none of them ran in any workflow before
items.title: Deploy can ship a revision that continuous integration rejected
items.userProblem: The live site can be running code that the pipeline says is broken, with nothing reporting a conflict.
items.source: external review (ChatGPT), confirmed against workflow files
acceptanceCriteria: deploy.yml will not deploy unless the CI verify job succeeded for that commit
An override exists, requires explicit intent and is recorded in the run log
Proven by pushing a commit with a deliberately failing check and observing deploy refuse
evidence: Deploy succeeded at least four times while CI was red
pages.yml already gates on needs.verify.result == success; deploy.yml is the outlier
Deploy gate omits check-ui.mjs, V2 unit tests, pages:test and root format:check, which is why both were green and red at once
Gate logic: 22 checks pass, 5 mutations each detected, restored clean
A stray shell command wrote a malformed-to-PASS mutation into the gate; the suite caught it
items.securityImpact: ships unreviewed code to the public origin
items.summary: Deployment could put code on the live site that the test pipeline had already rejected, because the two were checking different things. Now a deployment refuses unless the tests genuinely passed for that exact version.

items.title: Readers of canonical state may treat unreadable as empty
items.userProblem: A corrupt state file can silently downgrade a blocking condition into an all-clear.
items.source: defect found in release-gate.mjs during this project
acceptanceCriteria: Every reader of .ai/*.json distinguishes absent, valid and unparseable
Unparseable refuses; it is never reported as no findings
Each is mutation-tested with all three cases, malformed included
evidence: A corrupt findings.json made the release gate print PASS no open P0 or P1 and exit 0
release-gate.mjs is fixed; the other readers have not been audited
items.summary: Several internal checks read a status file and, if that file was damaged or unreadable, concluded there was nothing wrong. That is how a blocked release once reported itself ready. Every such reader needs to treat unreadable as a refusal.

items.title: V2 tests in CI cover no database, queue or browser path
items.userProblem: The layer where the application actually fails is the layer CI does not exercise.
acceptanceCriteria: Postgres and Redis service containers run in CI with a CI-built environment file
The six integration files execute rather than being skipped
A skipped suite is reported as not run, never as passed
evidence: Layer A is 33 unit tests; six files need real services
The CI step is named to say unit only so the gap is not misread
items.summary: The tests that need a real database, queue and browser do not run in the pipeline at all. That is the layer where this application actually breaks, so the current pipeline proves less than it appears to.

items.title: Twenty-four agents exist with no activation policy
items.userProblem: A roster nobody can route confidently becomes ceremony, and ceremony hides real review gaps.
acceptanceCriteria: Each agent is retained only if it produces a unique artefact, holds a distinct permission boundary, makes a materially different decision, or supplies independent evidence
A written activation policy states which agents a given change class requires
Agents failing the retention test are merged or removed, not left dormant
evidence: The roster grew 11 to 24 in one session
AGENT-SETUP.md described 11 agents for two cycles while the validator stayed green
items.summary: There are twenty-four defined review roles and nothing said how many should take part in a given change. An activation policy now sets a default of four; this item is the follow-up audit of which roles genuinely earn their place.

items.title: The public Pages surface has had no design pass
items.userProblem: The public job list is the only part of CareerScope a stranger ever sees, and it was built to be correct rather than to be read.
acceptanceCriteria: Hierarchy, type scale and spacing come from the design system, not ad-hoc values
Empty, loading, error and long-content states are designed, not incidental
Verified at real breakpoints including 768px, in all three browser engines
Accessibility verified with the accesslint-audit skill, not asserted
No new external origin, no build step, and the snapshot allowlist is unchanged
evidence: mobile-site/ and _site/ are plain HTML, CSS and ES modules with no design system applied
CS-2 shows breakpoint behaviour here is not currently trustworthy
items.securityImpact: public artifact — allowlist must not widen
items.summary: The public job page is the only part of CareerScope a stranger ever sees, and it was built to be correct rather than to be read. This is a proper design pass over it.

items.title: Agent invocation was believed impossible; it is not
items.userProblem: A system described as orchestrated, but driven by hand, misleads whoever reads its state next.
acceptanceCriteria: Documentation states that agents can be invoked and that sequencing is what remains manual
A daily routine exists that names which agent is invoked at which step
Agent output is recorded as a finding attributed to that agent, never as state claiming autonomous action
The read-only permission boundary is confirmed to hold under real invocation
evidence: All 24 agents WAITING, activity empty, every iteration counter 0, qa not-run, lastVerdict null
check-agents.mjs validates configuration only; it cannot observe execution
External review: manufacturing an end-to-end run would be worse than having no orchestration evidence
Code Quality agent invoked 2026-09-19: read scripts/agile.mjs, returned file:line findings, one of them a real defect
The false claim had already been committed to .github/copilot-instructions.md and .ai/AGENT-SETUP.md
items.securityImpact: none directly; removes assumed review assurance
items.summary: Two documents, and an external review built on them, stated that the specialist agents could not be run automatically. Running one disproved it in a single attempt — and that agent immediately found a real defect. What is actually manual is the sequencing between agents, not the invocation.

items.title: Signed-in screens have no shared loading, empty or error treatment
items.summary: Each screen invents its own behaviour while data is loading, when there is nothing to show, or when something fails. The result is that the product feels different from page to page, and some failures show nothing at all. One shared set of states fixes both.
items.userProblem: A screen that silently shows nothing is indistinguishable from a screen that is still loading.
acceptanceCriteria: One shared set of loading, empty and error components used by every signed-in route
Every error state says what failed and offers the next action, never a bare message
Empty states distinguish "nothing yet" from "nothing matches your filters"
Verified in all three browser engines at 320, 768 and 1440 widths
evidence: Each route currently implements its own handling; several have no error state
items.securityImpact: error text must not leak internal detail

items.title: The Leads table is unusable on a phone
items.summary: Leads is the screen you would actually use most, and on a narrow screen it is a wide table squeezed into a small space. It needs a layout designed for a phone rather than a shrunken desktop one.
items.userProblem: The most-used screen is the least usable on the device most likely to be at hand.
acceptanceCriteria: A layout designed for narrow widths, not a horizontally scrolled table
Score, title, company and status remain readable without zooming
No horizontal page overflow at 320px
Keyboard and screen-reader operable, verified not assumed
evidence: check-ui.mjs already asserts no overflow at 320px; readability is untested

items.title: No accessibility baseline has ever been measured
items.summary: Accessibility has been handled case by case with no measurement, so nobody knows the current state. This establishes a baseline with a real audit, fixes what it finds, and makes the result something a check can hold to.
items.userProblem: Unmeasured accessibility is indistinguishable from none.
acceptanceCriteria: Every signed-in route and the public Pages surface audited against WCAG 2.2 AA
Findings recorded with severity rather than summarised as a score
Blocking issues fixed; the rest become tracked items with reasons
A check enforces the baseline so it cannot regress silently
evidence: The accesslint-audit skill is installed and has not been run against this product

items.title: Discovery does not present jobs in a way you can act on
items.summary: Search returns matches, but the list gives you little more than a title and a number. You cannot tell from it which jobs are worth opening, so the ranking work behind it goes to waste.
items.userProblem: A ranked list you cannot skim is no better than an unranked one.
items.source: external review — first step of the core product slice
acceptanceCriteria: A result row shows enough to decide whether to open it: role, company, location, recency, salary when known, and why it matched
Filters that exist in the API are reachable from the UI
Ranking order is visible and explainable, never an unexplained number
Readable at 320, 768 and 1440 widths in all three engines
evidence: The matching package produces dimension scores that the UI does not surface

items.title: There is no job detail view worth opening
items.summary: Opening a job should tell you what the role is, what it pays, what it demands, and whether it is worth your time. Today that decision is made on a list row.
items.userProblem: Deciding to apply is the highest-stakes action here, made with the least information.
items.source: external review — second step of the core product slice
acceptanceCriteria: Full description, requirements, company, location, salary and source link
Original posting always reachable, and clearly marked as leaving the app
Untrusted posting content is rendered safely — no HTML injection from a job source
Save, dismiss and apply actions available without returning to the list
evidence: Job descriptions come from external sources and are attacker-influenced input
items.securityImpact: renders third-party content — sanitisation is mandatory

items.title: The match score is a number with no explanation
items.summary: Scoring weighs several dimensions and then shows you one number. Without seeing which parts matched and which did not, you cannot trust the score or correct your profile when it is wrong.
items.userProblem: An unexplained score is either believed blindly or ignored entirely. Both are wrong.
items.source: external review — third step of the core product slice
acceptanceCriteria: Per-dimension contributions shown, including the ones that scored badly
Hard exclusions state which rule excluded the job
Low-confidence results say so rather than presenting a confident-looking number
Presentation derives from the matching output; no second copy of the weights in the UI
evidence: Deterministic scoring with dimension weights, exclusion gates and a low-confidence ceiling already exists and is not surfaced
items.architectureImpact: must read weights from the matching package, not duplicate them

items.title: Saving a job and working the shortlist is not a coherent flow
items.summary: Finding a job is only useful if what happens next holds together: save it, find it again, move it through stages, and see what is waiting on you. That loop is what makes this a tool rather than a search box.
items.userProblem: Without a working shortlist, every search starts from nothing.
items.source: external review — final step of the core product slice
acceptanceCriteria: Save from both list and detail, with immediate confirmation and an undo
Status changes persist and survive a reload
The shortlist makes clear what is waiting on the user
A duplicate posting already saved is recognised, not saved twice
evidence: Fingerprint deduplication exists in discovery; the UI does not use it when saving
items.securityImpact: owner isolation must hold on every lead mutation

items.title: agile status and review reported a clean board from files they could not read
items.summary: The daily status command showed zero work in progress and zero blocking problems when the files holding that information were missing entirely. A clean board produced by an inability to look is the most dangerous output this project produces.
items.userProblem: A dashboard that cannot distinguish "nothing wrong" from "cannot see" is worse than no dashboard.
acceptanceCriteria: status and review refuse when backlog.json or findings.json is absent or unparseable
The refusal names the file and the reason
Covered by the agile gate mutation suite
evidence: read(path, { items: [] }) turned a missing backlog into an empty one at scripts/agile.mjs
Same defect class as the release-gate findings.json failure

items.title: Sprint carry could never mark anything finished
items.summary: The carry command I added counted a finished item by a status value that does not exist in this system, so a completed item would have been carried into the next week forever while the review command counted the same item as done.
items.userProblem: Two commands disagreeing about what "finished" means makes both untrustworthy.
acceptanceCriteria: One shared definition of complete used by review and carry
The value is one the status vocabulary actually contains
A released item is reported as completed by carry, not carried forward
evidence: carry compared against 'DONE'; review compares against 'RELEASED'; the status list contains only the latter
Introduced by me two commits before it was found
